speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiates to your jaw when you eat, which suggests referred pain; have you noticed any clicking, popping, or limited movement in your right jaw joint recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myofascial Pain Syndrome of the Lateral Pterygoid Muscle (referred to the ear) / Temporomandibular Joint Disorder.

The referred pain during eating and earring discomfort after a right-sided tympanoplasty, combined with your history of chronic ear infections and stress, strongly suggests tension from the lateral pterygoid muscle or TMJ dysfunction rather than a surgical complication or recurrent cholesteatoma. Given the 12-week post-op timeline and lack of fever or discharge, a malignant recurrence or infection is unlikely.

REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Temporal_Bone_Coronal to assess the middle ear space and mastoid air cells.
